title: Spectral bisection
text: Order the vertices, then sweep the cut
transcript: Build the Laplacian, solve for a Fiedler vector live and sweep legal thresholds.

title: Learning goals
text: Build L=D−A edge by edge · Verify row sums and the quadratic form · Explain the second eigenvector
transcript:
Build L=D−A edge by edge
Verify row sums and the quadratic form
Explain the second eigenvector
Report residuals and degeneracy
Sweep legal ordering prefixes
Recognize the limits of the relaxation

title: 01 · Use global structure to order vertices
text: Spectral bisection relaxes discrete labels into continuous coordinates, encourages strongly connected vertices to stay close, then converts coordinates back into a split.
transcript: Spectral bisection relaxes discrete labels into continuous coordinates, encourages strongly connected vertices to stay close, then converts coordinates back into a split. Here L=D−A is the unnormalized Laplacian. This is neither a normalized-cut implementation nor a physical spring simulation.

title: 02 · Build L edge by edge
text: For u–v of weight w, add w to Luu and Lvv and subtract w from Luv and Lvu.
transcript: For u–v of weight w, add w to Luu and Lvv and subtract w from Luv and Lvu. In G01, A has weighted degree 6, giving first row [6,−5,−1,0,0] in A–E order. The matrix is symmetric, has nonnegative diagonal and zero row sums.

title: 03 · The vector and its diagnostics
transcript: Sort eigenvalues increasingly. A connected graph has smallest eigenvalue 0 with a constant eigenvector. An eigenvector for the second smallest eigenvalue λ2 is a Fiedler vector. The page solves the symmetric problem live using Jacobi rotations and reports residual ‖Lx−λ2x‖/‖x‖, orthogonality to constants and the λ2–λ3 gap.

title: 04 · Sweep every legal prefix
text: Sort vertices by ascending coordinate and try prefixes of lengths 1 through n−1.
transcript: Sort vertices by ascending coordinate and try prefixes of lengths 1 through n−1. Check the count window and compute each cut. By default each side needs at least 20% of the vertices. This is a count rule, not an area bound.

title: 05 · Disconnection and repeated eigenvalues
text: Multiple connected components produce multiple zero eigenvalues and a non-unique second vector.
transcript: Multiple connected components produce multiple zero eigenvalues and a non-unique second vector. A connected graph can also have λ2=λ3; the equal-weight four-cycle has both equal to 2. Different valid solvers may return different directions in the same eigenspace.

title: 06 · A relaxation is not an exact solver
transcript: Continuous coordinates provide structural guidance. Prefix cuts cover only a small fraction of discrete assignments, and rounding must still satisfy balance. G01's optimum of 3 does not establish a general guarantee.

title: 07 · Implement two auditable stages
text: Implement laplacian and sweep_cut in Python.
transcript: Implement laplacian and sweep_cut in Python. The latter receives an explicit ordering and count window and returns the best legal prefix assignment. Separating numerical solution from discrete sweep makes both testable without requiring a complete eigensolver in an introductory exercise.

title: Decision contract
text: Build the Laplacian, solve for a Fiedler vector live and sweep legal thresholds.

title: Check the common mistakes
transcript: Sweep legal prefixes: G01 cuts are 6,3,5,6.

title: Test your understanding
text: Predict → run the lab → solve challenges → write two Python functions
transcript: Explain your reasoning with actual output, the objective, constraints and stop reason.
